def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a field ([[def-field]]), and let $V_1,\ldots,V_n$ be graded
$k$-vector spaces. A $k$-vector space is a unital left $k$-module as in
[[def-left-and-right-modules]]. Tensor powers are formed using the tensor
products of
[[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]]. If $f_i:V_i\to W_i$ are homogeneous
linear maps of degrees $d_i$, and $x_i\in V_i$ are homogeneous of degrees
$p_i$, the graded tensor map is defined on pure tensors by

$$(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)(x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_n) =(-1)^{\sum_{i>j}d_i p_j} f_1(x_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n(x_n).$$

It is extended linearly. In particular, for two maps,
$(f\otimes g)(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{|g||x|}f(x)\otimes g(y)$.

For homogeneous $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ and a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$, the
**Koszul sign** of reordering them to
$x_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{\sigma(n)}$ is

$$\epsilon(\sigma;x_1,\ldots,x_n) =(-1)^{\sum_{\substack{i<j\\\sigma(i)>\sigma(j)}} |x_{\sigma(i)}||x_{\sigma(j)}|}.$$

Thus swapping two adjacent homogeneous factors $x,y$ contributes
$(-1)^{|x||y|}$. Every tensor of maps, permutation, unshuffle, and symmetric
power below uses this same convention. A sign is a scalar in $k$ determined
only by the parity of the displayed integer exponent.
def-triple-massey-data:
## Definition

Let $(A,d,\mu)$ be a cohomological differential graded algebra over a
commutative ring, with the degree-one differential and signed Leibniz rule of
[[def-differential-graded-algebra]]. For $j\in\mathbb Z$, define

$$H^j(A)=\ker(d:A^j\to A^{j+1})/\operatorname{im}(d:A^{j-1}\to A^j).$$

A **triple Massey datum** consists of homogeneous closed elements
$a\in A^p$, $b\in A^q$, and $c\in A^r$ such that $ab$ and $bc$ are boundaries,
together with elements

$$u\in A^{p+q-1},\qquad v\in A^{q+r-1},\qquad du=ab,\quad dv=bc.$$

The associated **triple Massey expression** is

$$\omega(a,b,c;u,v)=(-1)^{p+1}av+uc\in A^{p+q+r-1}.$$

This item defines the data and expression only. The next lemma proves that the
expression is closed, so its cohomology class is defined.
def-a-infinity-algebra:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a field ([[def-field]]) and let
$A=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbb Z}A^j$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$-graded $k$-vector space; its tensor
maps use the convention in [[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]]. An
**uncurved cohomological A∞-algebra in the unsuspended convention** is a
sequence of homogeneous $k$-linear maps

$$m_n:A^{\otimes_k n}\longrightarrow A,\qquad |m_n|=2-n, \qquad n\ge1,$$

such that for every $n\ge1$ the following equality of maps
$A^{\otimes_k n}\to A$ holds:

$$\sum_{\substack{r,t\ge0,\ s\ge1\\r+s+t=n}} (-1)^{r+st} m_{r+1+t}\bigl(1^{\otimes r}\otimes m_s\otimes1^{\otimes t}\bigr)=0.$$

Here $1$ denotes the identity map of $A$, the tensor maps use the Koszul rule,
and the displayed sign $(-1)^{r+st}$ is part of the fixed convention. The
degree condition means that for homogeneous inputs of degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_n$,
$m_n$ has output degree $j_1+\cdots+j_n+2-n$.

“Uncurved” means no arity-zero operation $m_0$ is included. “Nonunital” means
that no unit is part of this definition. A unit or a strict-unit condition on
higher operations is additional data and must be stated separately. No graded
commutativity is assumed for $m_2$.
lem-triple-massey-expression-is-closed:
## Statement

For every triple Massey datum in
[[def-triple-massey-data]], the expression
$\omega=(-1)^{p+1}av+uc$ is closed. Thus it determines a class in
$H^{p+q+r-1}(A)$.
def-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field ([[def-field]]), meaning
$\operatorname{char}(k)=0$ under [[def-ring-characteristic]]. By
[[lem-field-is-a-commutative-ring]], $k$ is a commutative ring. Let
$W=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbb Z}W^j$ be a graded $k$-vector space. For $n\ge1$,
define the graded symmetric power

$$S^n(W)=W^{\otimes_k n}/J_n,$$

where $J_n$ is spanned by the differences obtained by replacing any adjacent
homogeneous factors $x\otimes y$ by
$(-1)^{|x||y|}y\otimes x$ inside a pure tensor. Write
$w_1\odot\cdots\odot w_n$ for the image of a tensor and set

$$S^c(W)=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}S^n(W).$$

The **reduced shuffle coproduct** is the degree-zero linear map
$\bar\Delta:S^c(W)\to S^c(W)\otimes_k S^c(W)$ given on a homogeneous pure
symmetric tensor by

$$\bar\Delta(w_1\odot\cdots\odot w_n) =\sum_{p=1}^{n-1}\ \sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Sh}(p,n-p)} \epsilon(\sigma;w_1,\ldots,w_n) (w_{\sigma(1)}\odot\cdots\odot w_{\sigma(p)})\otimes (w_{\sigma(p+1)}\odot\cdots\odot w_{\sigma(n)}),$$

where
$\operatorname{Sh}(p,n-p)=\{\sigma\in S_n:\sigma(1)<\cdots<\sigma(p),\
\sigma(p+1)<\cdots<\sigma(n)\}$, and $\epsilon$ is the Koszul sign of
[[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]].
For $n=1$ the sum is empty and $\bar\Delta(w)=0$. This is a reduced, hence
noncounital coalgebra convention; no arity-zero summand is included. The next
lemmas verify its coproduct laws, conilpotence, and cofree universal property.
def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $B$ be a commutative unital $k$-algebra concentrated in degree zero, and let $I$ be an ideal such that $B\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}B/I^n$. Nilpotent ideals are included. Let $V$ be any graded $k$-vector space; no finite-dimensionality assumption is made. Use the graded tensor convention of [[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]].

The carrier $C$ is either the coaugmented tensor coalgebra $T^c(V)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}V^{\otimes r}$ with deconcatenation, or the coaugmented graded symmetric coalgebra $S^c(V)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}S^r(V)$ with unshuffle coproduct. For the latter, $S^r$ means graded symmetric coinvariants, and the coproduct sums over all divisions of the inputs into two ordered sublists, with the Koszul sign. The empty word is $1_C$, the counit $\epsilon$ is projection to length zero, and the coaugmentation is inclusion of scalars. These formulas specify the carrier without requiring a cofree universal property.

Define its coefficient completion, filtration, and tensor target by

$$C_B=\varprojlim_n(C\otimes_k B/I^n),\qquad F^nC_B=\ker(C_B\longrightarrow C\otimes_k B/I^n),\qquad F^0C_B=C_B.$$

$$C_B\widehat\otimes_B C_B=\varprojlim_n((C\otimes_k C)\otimes_k B/I^n).$$

All inverse limits in this definition are in graded modules: explicitly $(C_B)^j=\varprojlim_n(C^j\otimes_k B/I^n)$ and $C_B=\bigoplus_j(C_B)^j$, and the tensor target is completed in each fixed total degree. All structure maps are extended degreewise through these inverse limits. This is coefficient completion of a direct sum: modulo each $I^n$ every element has finite length support. No unrestricted product over arities is included. Completed tensor powers and polynomial coefficients mean the analogous explicit inverse limits. A homogeneous map is understood in the grading induced by $C$, and continuity always means the displayed coefficient topology.

Let $E^d$ consist of continuous $B$-linear filtration-preserving homogeneous endomorphisms of degree $d$ on $C_B$, and set $E=\bigoplus_d E^d$, with composition $E^dE^e\subseteq E^{d+e}$. Completeness of this graded composition algebra always means completeness of each $E^d$ separately, not of its ungraded direct sum. All exponential and logarithm series below have inputs in $E^0$ and remain in $E^0$; their conjugation series on a homogeneous $T\in E^d$ remain in that same fixed $E^d$. Its order filtration is

$$F^pE=\{T:T(F^qC_B)\subseteq F^{p+q}C_B\text{ for every }q\ge0\}\quad(p\ge0).$$

Let $\mathfrak l\subset E$ be the homogeneous coderivations satisfying $T(1_C)=0$, $\epsilon T=0$, and

$$\Delta T=(T\otimes1+1\otimes T)\Delta.$$

The sign in $1\otimes T$ is the graded tensor sign. In particular these coderivations have zero nullary component. Fix $D\in\mathfrak l^1$ with $D^2=0$. A **coefficient-complete fixed-carrier codifferential deformation** is $D+R$ with $R\in F^1\mathfrak l^1$ and $(D+R)^2=0$. Its allowed equivalences are degree-zero continuous $B$-linear counital coaugmented coalgebra automorphisms $G$ such that $G-\operatorname{id}\in F^1E$, acting by $D+R\mapsto G(D+R)G^{-1}$.

Here identity modulo $I$ can equivalently be stated as $(G-\operatorname{id})(C_B)\subseteq F^1C_B$. To see the filtration implication without assuming that $I$ is finitely generated, observe that $F^qC_B$ is the closure of $C\otimes I^q$: modulo $F^n$, $n>q$, every element lifts from $C\otimes I^q$. By $B$-linearity a continuous map with image in $F^1$ carries that dense submodule into $F^{q+1}$; closedness gives the same inclusion on all $F^q$.

This contract uses all continuous coefficient-complete Taylor operations. It does not identify them with a naive algebraic tensor $\operatorname{Hom}_k(W,U)\otimes I$ when the coefficient algebra is infinite dimensional. Over a finite-dimensional coefficient algebra, expanding in a finite coefficient basis does give the usual tensor identification, without any finite-dimensionality assumption on $W,U$.
lem-low-arity-stasheff-identities:
## Statement

Let $(A,m_n)$ be an uncurved cohomological A∞-algebra with the unsuspended
convention of [[def-a-infinity-algebra]]. Its first three identities are

$$m_1m_1=0,$$

$$m_1m_2=m_2(m_1\otimes1+1\otimes m_1),$$

and

$$m_1m_3+m_3(m_1\otimes1\otimes1+1\otimes m_1\otimes1+1\otimes1\otimes m_1) +m_2(m_2\otimes1)-m_2(1\otimes m_2)=0.$$

In particular, $m_1$ is a cochain differential and a signed derivation of
$m_2$. The third identity explicitly gives the associator
$m_2(m_2\otimes1)-m_2(1\otimes m_2)$ as the negative of the displayed
$m_1,m_3$ terms.
def-a-infinity-morphism:
## Definition

Let $A$ and $B$ be uncurved cohomological A∞-algebras in the convention of
[[def-a-infinity-algebra]]. An **A∞-morphism** $f:A\to B$ is a family of
homogeneous maps

$$f_n:A^{\otimes_k n}\longrightarrow B,\qquad |f_n|=1-n,\qquad n\ge1,$$

such that, for every $n\ge1$, the following equality of maps
$A^{\otimes_k n}\to B$ holds:

$$\sum_{\substack{r,s,t\ge0,\ s\ge1\\r+s+t=n}} (-1)^{r+st}f_{r+1+t}(1^{\otimes r}\otimes m_s^A\otimes1^{\otimes t}) =\sum_{q=1}^{n}\ \sum_{\substack{i_1+\cdots+i_q=n\\i_j\ge1}} (-1)^{\eta(i_1,\ldots,i_q)} m_q^B(f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_q}),$$

where
$\eta(i_1,\ldots,i_q)=\sum_{j=1}^{q-1}(q-j)(i_j-1)$ and all tensor maps
use [[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]]. The identity at $n=1$ says
that $f_1$ is a cochain map from $(A,m_1^A)$ to $(B,m_1^B)$.

An A∞-morphism is an **A∞ quasi-isomorphism** if $f_1$ induces an isomorphism
on cohomology, where
$H^j(A,m_1^A)=\ker(m_1^A:A^j\to A^{j+1})/\operatorname{im}(m_1^A:A^{j-1}\to A^j)$
and likewise for $B$. This definition imposes no unit condition on $f$.
def-triple-massey-product:
## Definition

Let $A$ and its cohomology groups be as in [[def-triple-massey-data]], and let
$\alpha\in H^p(A)$, $\beta\in H^q(A)$ and $\gamma\in H^r(A)$ be cohomology
classes. Their **triple Massey product** in that item's sign convention is the
subset

$$\langle\alpha,\beta,\gamma\rangle =\{[\omega(a,b,c;u,v)]\in H^{p+q+r-1}(A): (a,b,c;u,v)\text{ is a triple Massey datum representing }(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\}.$$

The expression is a cohomology class because it is closed by
[[lem-triple-massey-expression-is-closed]]. The set includes every choice of
cocycle representatives and null-homotopies for which the adjacent products
are boundaries; if there is no such datum, it is empty. No claim that the set
is a singleton is part of the definition.
lem-shuffle-coproduct-coassociative-coco:
## Statement

Let $S^c(W)$ and $\bar\Delta$ be as in
[[def-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra]]. The reduced coproduct is
well-defined on the graded-symmetric quotient, is coassociative and
graded-cocommutative, and is conilpotent: every element is killed by a
sufficiently long iterated reduced coproduct. Its primitive subspace
($\ker\bar\Delta$) is exactly $S^1(W)=W$.
lem-complete-coderivations-form-a-filter:
## Statement

Use [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]]. For every fixed degree $d$, the order filtration on $E^d$ is separated and complete, with $E^d\cong\varprojlim_n E^d/(F^nE)^d$; thus $E$ is complete as a graded algebra in the degreewise sense, with $F^pE\,F^qE\subseteq F^{p+q}E$. The coderivations form a closed graded Lie subalgebra for

$$[P,Q]=PQ-(-1)^{|P||Q|}QP.$$

With $dT=[D,T]$, the positive-order space $\mathfrak g=F^1\mathfrak l$ is a complete filtered differential graded Lie algebra in this degreewise sense, with $F^p\mathfrak g=F^p\mathfrak l$ for $p\ge1$, $d(F^p\mathfrak g)\subseteq F^p\mathfrak g$, and $[F^p\mathfrak g,F^q\mathfrak g]\subseteq F^{p+q}\mathfrak g$.
lem-noncommutative-filtered-exponential-:
## Statement

Let $E$ be any unital associative $k$-algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with descending two-sided filtration $F^0E=E$, $F^pE\,F^qE\subseteq F^{p+q}E$, and $E\cong\varprojlim E/F^nE$. Commutativity is not assumed. The formulas

$$\exp X=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{X^j}{j!},\qquad \log(1+N)=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{j-1}N^j}{j}$$

give mutually inverse bijections $F^1E\leftrightarrow1+F^1E$, and $\exp(-X)$ is the inverse of $\exp X$. For $X\in F^1E$ and $T\in E$,

$$\exp(X)T\exp(-X)=\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{(\operatorname{ad}_X)^r(T)}{r!},\qquad \operatorname{ad}_X(T)=XT-TX.$$

There is also a degreewise-complete graded variant: assume $E=\bigoplus_dE^d$ is a multiplicatively filtered graded algebra with each $E^d\cong\varprojlim_n E^d/(F^nE)^d$. Then exp and log give inverse bijections $(F^1E)^0\leftrightarrow1+(F^1E)^0$, and the displayed conjugation identity holds for $X\in(F^1E)^0$ and any fixed homogeneous $T\in E^d$. The first two series converge in $E^0$ and the conjugation series in $E^d$; no completeness of the ungraded direct sum is required. In particular this variant applies to the degreewise complete endomorphism algebra in [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]] once its completeness is established.
prop-differential-graded-algebra-induces:
## Statement

Let $k$ be a field and let $(A,d,\mu)$ be a cohomological differential graded
algebra over $k$ in the convention of
[[def-differential-graded-algebra]]. Put $m_1=d$, $m_2=\mu$, and $m_n=0$ for
all $n\ge3$. Then these maps make $A$ an uncurved cohomological A∞-algebra
in the unsuspended convention of [[def-a-infinity-algebra]].
def-minimal-a-infinity-model:
## Definition

Let $A$ be an uncurved A∞-algebra ([[def-a-infinity-algebra]]). A
**minimal A∞-model** for $A$ is an
uncurved A∞-algebra $H$ with $m_1^H=0$, together with an A∞
quasi-isomorphism $f:H\to A$. Here an A∞ quasi-isomorphism is as defined in
[[def-a-infinity-morphism]]. In an explicit model whose underlying graded
space is identified with $H^*(A,m_1^A)$, the binary product is ordinarily
checked against the product induced by $m_2^A$; this definition does not
assert an existence or transfer theorem.

This is a definition of the data required for a minimal model. It does not
assert that every A∞-algebra has one or that a transfer theorem has been
proved.
lem-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra-i:
## Statement

Let $W$ be a graded vector space over a characteristic-zero field and let
$S^c(W)$ be the reduced graded symmetric coalgebra of
[[def-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra]]. Let $C$ be any graded
$k$-vector space with a degree-zero reduced coproduct
$\bar\Delta_C:C\to C\otimes_k C$ that is coassociative and graded-cocommutative
(invariant under the graded flip), with no counit. Assume that for every
$c\in C$ some iterated reduced coproduct of $c$ is zero; such a coalgebra is
called **conilpotent** here. A coalgebra morphism is a degree-zero linear map
commuting with the reduced coproduct.
For any degree-zero linear map $\phi:C\to W$, there is a unique degree-zero
coalgebra morphism $G:C\to S^c(W)$ whose length-one projection is $\phi$.
Explicitly, let $\rho_n:W^{\otimes n}\to S^n(W)$ be the quotient map, put
$\bar\Delta_C^{(0)}=\operatorname{id}_C$, and define iterates recursively by
$\bar\Delta_C^{(n)}=(\bar\Delta_C^{(n-1)}\otimes1)\bar\Delta_C$; coassociativity
makes the parenthesization immaterial. Then

$$G(c)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{n!}\rho_n\!\left( \phi^{\otimes n}\bar\Delta_C^{(n-1)}(c)\right).$$

The sum is finite for each $c$ by conilpotence. In particular, the graded
symmetric coalgebra is the reduced cofree conilpotent cocommutative coalgebra
on $W$.
lem-coderivation-extension-from-corestri:
## Statement

Let $W$ and $S^c(W)$ be as in
[[def-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra]]. For any family of degree $+1$
graded-symmetric maps $q_n:S^n(W)\to W$, $n\ge1$, the formula

$$Q(w_1\odot\cdots\odot w_N) =\sum_{n=1}^{N}\ \sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Sh}(n,N-n)} \epsilon(\sigma;w_1,\ldots,w_N) q_n(w_{\sigma(1)}\odot\cdots\odot w_{\sigma(n)})\odot w_{\sigma(n+1)}\odot\cdots\odot w_{\sigma(N)}$$

defines a degree $+1$ coderivation of $S^c(W)$. It is the unique such
coderivation whose projection to $S^1(W)=W$ on $S^n(W)$ is $q_n$.
For $n=N$, the final tail is empty and the term means just
$q_N(w_{\sigma(1)}\odot\cdots\odot w_{\sigma(N)})$; in this case
$\operatorname{Sh}(N,0)$ contains only the identity permutation.

Here a degree-one **coderivation** is a linear map $Q:S^c(W)\to S^c(W)$ that
satisfies

$$\bar\Delta Q=(Q\otimes1+1\otimes Q)\bar\Delta,$$

where the tensor map $1\otimes Q$ uses the Koszul sign rule. The sum defining
$Q$ is finite on each input because $n\le N$.
lem-unsuspended-a-infinity-identities-ar:
## Statement

Let $A$ be a graded vector space over a field and let $m_n:A^{\otimes n}\to A$ have degree $2-n$, $n\ge1$. Use the Koszul tensor-map convention of [[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]]. Write $X=A[1]$, $X^j=A^{j+1}$, and let $s_A:A\to X$ have degree $-1$ with inverse $u_A$ of degree $+1$. Put $c_n=n(n-1)/2$ and define

$$b_n=(-1)^{c_n}s_A m_n u_A^{\otimes n}:X^{\otimes n}\longrightarrow X.$$

Equivalently $b_n s_A^{\otimes n}=s_A m_n$ and $m_n=u_A b_n s_A^{\otimes n}$. Each $b_n$ has degree one. On homogeneous elements this formula reads

$$b_n(s_Aa_1,\ldots,s_Aa_n)=(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^n(n-j)|a_j|}s_A m_n(a_1,\ldots,a_n).$$

Define the reduced tensor coalgebra $T^c(X)=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}X^{\otimes n}$ with reduced deconcatenation, and its coaugmented version $T^c_+(X)=k\cdot1\oplus T^c(X)$ with

$$\Delta(x_1\cdots x_N)=\sum_{i=0}^N(x_1\cdots x_i)\otimes(x_{i+1}\cdots x_N).$$

Empty words mean $1$. The $b_n$ extend uniquely to a degree-one coderivation $B:T^c_+(X)\to T^c_+(X)$ with $B(1)=0$, zero counit and corestrictions $b_n$. Explicitly

$$B|_{X^{\otimes N}}=\sum_{r+s+t=N\atop r,t\ge0,\ s\ge1}1^{\otimes r}\otimes b_s\otimes1^{\otimes t}.$$

Then $B^2=0$ if and only if the $m_n$ satisfy precisely the unsuspended A∞ identities of [[def-a-infinity-algebra]], with sign $(-1)^{r+st}$ in every arity. This gives a bijection between those uncurved structures and such square-zero coderivations. The same correspondence holds after removing the coaugmentation summand. No arity-zero operation or tensor completion is included.

Moreover, for structures on $A,D$ and homogeneous maps $f_n:A^{\otimes n}\to D$ of degree $1-n$, define degree-zero maps

$$F_n=(-1)^{c_n}s_D f_n u_A^{\otimes n}.$$

They extend uniquely to a coaugmentation- and counit-preserving coalgebra map $F:T^c_+(A[1])\to T^c_+(D[1])$, and $FB_A=B_DF$ if and only if $f$ satisfies exactly [[def-a-infinity-morphism]], including its right-hand sign

$$\eta(i_1,\ldots,i_q)=\sum_{j=1}^{q-1}(q-j)(i_j-1).$$

Composition of these coalgebra maps corresponds to the unsuspended Taylor composition $h_N=\sum_{q,\ i_1+\cdots+i_q=N}(-1)^\eta g_q(f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_q})$. In particular the correspondence respects identities.

The fixed signs give $b_1=s_A m_1u_A$ and $b_2=-s_A m_2(u_A\otimes u_A)$. The latter is an equality of graded maps: evaluated on $s_Aa\otimes s_Ab$ it is $(-1)^{|a|}s_A m_2(a,b)$. Replacing every $b_n$ simultaneously by $-b_n$ preserves both the square-zero condition and the morphism equation when done on both algebras; changing just one arity is not part of this correspondence.
thm-coalgebra-automorphism-logarithms-ar:
## Statement

For the coefficient-complete tensor or symmetric carrier in [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]], exponential and logarithm restrict to mutually inverse bijections

$$F^1\mathfrak l^0\ \longleftrightarrow\ \{G:\ G\text{ is an allowed identity-modulo-}I\text{ coalgebra automorphism}\}.$$

In particular the logarithm of every such automorphism is a continuous counital coaugmentation-preserving coderivation; no finite-dimensionality or algebraic nilpotence of $I$ is required.
def-shifted-coalgebra-l-infinity-algebra:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field ([[def-field]],
[[def-ring-characteristic]]), and let $V=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbb Z}V^j$ be a
graded $k$-vector space. Use the cohomological suspension

$$W=V[1],\qquad W^j=V^{j+1}.$$

The reduced cofree conilpotent cocommutative coalgebra on $W$ is the
$S^c(W)=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}S^n(W)$ of
[[def-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra]], with its cofree property proved
in [[lem-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra-is-cofree]].

An **L∞-algebra on $V$ in the shifted coalgebra convention** is a degree $+1$
coderivation $Q:S^c(W)\to S^c(W)$ with $Q^2=0$ and no arity-zero component.
A coderivation satisfies
$\bar\Delta Q=(Q\otimes1+1\otimes Q)\bar\Delta$, with the Koszul sign on
$1\otimes Q$, as defined in
[[lem-coderivation-extension-from-corestrictions]]. Its corestrictions are

$$q_n=\pi_1 Q|_{S^n(W)}:S^n(W)\longrightarrow W,\qquad |q_n|=+1 \quad(n\ge1),$$

where $\pi_1:S^c(W)\to S^1(W)=W$ is the length-one projection. Conversely,
each such family determines a unique coderivation by that lemma. The
condition $Q^2=0$ is equivalent to the higher Jacobi identities proved in
[[lem-square-zero-coderivation-is-higher-jacobi-identities]].

This is the shifted convention only: no unsuspended skew operations $l_n$ or
translation formula for them is asserted. Curved $L_\infty$ structures with
an arity-zero term are outside this definition.
lem-square-zero-coderivation-is-higher-j:
## Statement

Let $Q$ be the degree-one coderivation of
[[def-shifted-coalgebra-l-infinity-algebra]], with corestrictions
$q_i:S^i(W)\to W$. For each $n\ge1$, define

$$J_n(w_1,\ldots,w_n) =\sum_{i=1}^{n}\ \sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Sh}(i,n-i)} \epsilon(\sigma;w_1,\ldots,w_n)\, q_{n-i+1}\!\left( q_i(w_{\sigma(1)}\odot\cdots\odot w_{\sigma(i)}) \odot w_{\sigma(i+1)}\odot\cdots\odot w_{\sigma(n)} \right),$$

where $\operatorname{Sh}(n,0)$ contains only the identity and an empty tail
after $q_i$ is omitted. Then $Q^2=0$ if and only if
$J_n(w_1,\ldots,w_n)=0$ for every $n$ and all homogeneous $w_j\in W$. These
are the shifted higher Jacobi identities; for $n=1$ the identity is
$q_1^2=0$.
def-complete-filtered-l-infinity-algebra:
## Definition

Let $(V,Q)$ be an L∞-algebra in the shifted convention of
[[def-shifted-coalgebra-l-infinity-algebra]], with $W=V[1]$ and corestrictions
$q_n:S^n(W)\to W$. A **complete filtered L∞-algebra** is this data together
with a descending filtration by graded subspaces

$$F^1W\supseteq F^2W\supseteq F^3W\supseteq\cdots$$

such that both of the following conditions hold:

1. For every fixed degree $j$, the natural map from $W^j$ to the compatible homogeneous cosets
   $$(w_r+(F^rW)^j)_{r\ge1},\qquad w_r\in W^j,\qquad w_{r+1}-w_r\in(F^rW)^j,$$
   is a bijection. Thus the filtration is separated and complete in each degree: $W^j\cong\varprojlim_r W^j/(F^rW)^j$. All graded inverse limits here and in the filtered Maurer–Cartan constructions are taken degreewise. The underlying graded space remains $\bigoplus_jW^j$; completeness does not assert convergence of sums of terms in unboundedly varying degrees.
2. For every $n\ge1$ and positive integers $r_1,\ldots,r_n$,
   $$q_n(F^{r_1}W,\ldots,F^{r_n}W) \subseteq F^{r_1+\cdots+r_n}W.$$

This definition imposes an algebraic filtration topology only; it makes no
analytic convergence assertion. The next theorem proves that the
Maurer–Cartan series converges for each $w\in F^1W^0$.
thm-filtered-l-infinity-maurer-cartan-se:
## Statement

Let $W$ be the shifted graded space of a complete filtered L∞-algebra over a
characteristic-zero field, and let $w\in F^1W^0$. Then the series

$$\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{n!}q_n(w,\ldots,w)$$

converges uniquely in the filtration topology to an element of $W^1$.
def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism:
## Definition

Let $W=V[1]$ and $Z=U[1]$ be the shifted spaces of two complete filtered L∞-algebras over the same characteristic-zero field, in the convention of [[def-complete-filtered-l-infinity-algebra]]. Write $Q,R$ for their degree-one square-zero coderivations and $q_n,r_n$ for their corestrictions. A **filtered L∞-morphism** from $W$ to $Z$ consists of degree-zero graded symmetric maps $f_n:S^nW\to Z$, $n\ge1$, with

$$f_n(F^{i_1}W,\ldots,F^{i_n}W)\subseteq F^{i_1+\cdots+i_n}Z\qquad(i_j\ge1),$$

whose associated coaugmented coalgebra map $F:k\oplus S^c(W)\to k\oplus S^c(Z)$ satisfies $FQ=RF$, after extending $Q,R$ by $Q(1)=R(1)=0$. There is no constant Taylor coefficient: $F(1)=1$. Explicitly, for homogeneous inputs,

$$F(x_1\cdots x_n)=\sum_{s=1}^n\frac1{s!}\sum_{(B_1,\ldots,B_s)}\epsilon(B_1,\ldots,B_s;x)\,f_{|B_1|}(x_{B_1})\cdots f_{|B_s|}(x_{B_s}).$$

The inner sum runs over ordered partitions of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ into nonempty blocks. Inside each block retain the original input order; $\epsilon$ is the Koszul sign of the permutation which lists those blocks in the indicated order. The factor $1/s!$ removes ordering of the graded symmetric output blocks. The length-one projection of $F$ on $S^nW$ is $f_n$.

The composite of $f:W\to Z$ and $g:Z\to T$ has associated map $GF$; its Taylor coefficients are the length-one projections of $GF$. The identity has $f_1=\operatorname{id}$ and $f_n=0$ for $n>1$. These definitions do not require $F^1W=W$. The complete positive ideal $P=F^1W$ is the space on which completed exponentials and Maurer–Cartan sums will be used.
def-maurer-cartan-element-of-complete-fi:
## Definition

For a complete filtered L∞-algebra in the convention of
[[def-complete-filtered-l-infinity-algebra]], a **Maurer–Cartan element** is
an element $w\in F^1W^0$ satisfying

$$\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{n!}q_n(w,\ldots,w)=0.$$

The series is the unique limit proved in
[[thm-filtered-l-infinity-maurer-cartan-series-converges]]. This equation
defines a set of solutions; it does not by itself specify a deformation
problem or an equivalence relation on those solutions.
lem-filtered-l-infinity-taylor-map-exten:
## Statement

Let $f:W\to Z$ be a filtered L∞-morphism as in [[def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism]], and put $P=F^1W$, $P'=F^1Z$. On $C(P)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S^nP$, including $S^0P=k\cdot1$, use the symmetric multiplication and the counital coproduct

$$\Delta(x_1\cdots x_n)=\sum_{I\sqcup J=\{1,\ldots,n\}}\epsilon(I,J;x)x_I\otimes x_J.$$

Empty subsets are allowed. Define $\mathcal F^NC(P)$ as the span of products $x_1\cdots x_n$ with $x_j\in F^{i_j}W$, all $i_j\ge1$, and $\sum_j i_j\ge N$; scalars have weight zero. Define the **completed coaugmented symmetric coalgebra**

$$\widehat C(P)=\varprojlim_N C(P)/\mathcal F^NC(P).$$

All completions and limits are degreewise. Complete tensor products for coproducts with the sum of the two weight filtrations. Then multiplication, coproduct, counit and coaugmentation extend continuously, as do $Q$ and the Taylor map $F$. Their continuous extensions satisfy $Q^2=0$, $\Delta F=(F\widehat\otimes F)\Delta$, and $FQ=RF$. The length-one projection extends continuously to $p_P:\widehat C(P)\to P$.

For $w\in P^0$ and homogeneous $v\in F^pW$, $p\ge1$, define the convergent expressions

$$e^w=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{w^n}{n!},\qquad c_q(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(w^n)}{n!},\qquad u=f_*(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{f_n(w^n)}{n!}.$$

They satisfy

$$\Delta e^w=e^w\otimes e^w,\qquad e^we^{-w}=1,\qquad Q(e^w)=c_q(w)e^w,\qquad F(e^w)=e^u,$$

and the marked-input identity

$$F(ve^w)=\left(\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{f_{n+1}(w^n,v)}{n!}\right)e^u.$$

This is a total filtration weight completion on the positive ideal, not an unspecified product by symmetric arity on all of $W$.
thm-filtered-l-infinity-morphisms-preser:
## Statement

Let $f:W\to Z$ be a filtered L∞-morphism between complete filtered algebras over a characteristic-zero field. For every $w\in F^1W^0$, the Taylor series $f_*(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}f_n(w^n)/n!$ converges in $F^1Z^0$, and its curvature satisfies

$$c_r(f_*(w))=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac1{n!}f_{n+1}(w^n,c_q(w)),\qquad c_q(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(w^n)}{n!}.$$

Consequently $f_*$ defines an actual continuous map $\operatorname{MC}(W)\to\operatorname{MC}(Z)$, with Maurer–Cartan elements as in [[def-maurer-cartan-element-of-complete-filtered-l-infinity-algebra]]. If $g:Z\to T$ is another filtered L∞-morphism, the composite $h=g\circ f$ has Taylor coefficients

$$h_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{s=1}^n\frac1{s!}\sum_{(B_1,\ldots,B_s)}\epsilon(B_1,\ldots,B_s;x)\,g_s\bigl(f_{|B_1|}(x_{B_1}),\ldots,f_{|B_s|}(x_{B_s})\bigr),$$

where blocks and signs are as in [[def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism]]. The composite is filtered, and

$$(g\circ f)_*(w)=g_*(f_*(w)).$$

Identity morphisms act as identities. These are equalities of convergent elements, not merely formal Taylor expressions; no quasi-isomorphism hypothesis is needed.
def-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-path:
## Definition

Let $W$ be a complete filtered shifted L∞-algebra over a characteristic-zero field $k$. Put $P=F^1W$ with its induced filtration. This is closed and complete in each degree: it is the kernel of $W\to W/F^1W$, and compatible cosets in $P/F^pW$ have their unique $W$-limit in that kernel. All $q_n$ preserve $P$.

The **completed polynomial coefficients** and **completed polynomial differential forms** mean

$$P[t]^{\wedge}=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t],\qquad P\widehat\otimes\Omega=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t,dt],\quad |t|=0,\quad |dt|=1.$$

These are compatible polynomials in each quotient; their degrees need not have a common bound. Evaluation at $0,1$, differentiation, and integration from $0$ to $t$ are defined in every quotient by polynomial formulas and commute with reduction; integration uses $\int_0^t u^jdu=t^{j+1}/(j+1)$. Operations on these spaces are extended continuously, with each coefficient of a fixed quotient a finite sum.

Write $C(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}q_n(w^n)/n!$ and $q_1^w(a)=\sum_{n\ge0}q_{n+1}(w^n,a)/n!$. An **elementary gauge path** is a pair $w\in P^0[t]^{\wedge}$, $a\in P^{-1}[t]^{\wedge}$ such that $C(w)=0$ and $w'=q_1^w(a)$. Its endpoints are $w(0),w(1)$. **Gauge equivalence** is the equivalence relation generated by endpoints of these paths. A constant path has $a=0$; reversal is $(w(1-t),-a(1-t))$; finite chains give transitivity. Polynomial concatenation is not required.

For the polynomial-form interpretation, forms are placed on the right. For homogeneous $x_i\in P$, $\alpha_i\in\Omega$, the extension of $q_n$ has scalar sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|\alpha_i||x_j|}$; its unary part also contains $(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes d\alpha$. The degree-zero form $z=w-a\,dt$ then satisfies $C_{\Omega}(z)=C(w)+(w'-q_1^w(a))dt$. Thus these paths are precisely Maurer–Cartan elements over the completed polynomial interval. This fixes a gauge construction using the full operations, rather than choosing an arbitrary equivalence relation on a solution set.
lem-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-equatio:
## Statement

In the setting of [[def-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-path]], for every $w_*\in\operatorname{MC}(P)$ and every $a\in P^{-1}[t]^{\wedge}$ there is a unique $w\in P^0[t]^{\wedge}$ with $w(0)=w_*$ and $w'=q_1^w(a)$. It satisfies $C(w)=0$, so it is an elementary gauge path. Modulo every $F^pW$ the construction stabilizes after finitely many polynomial Picard iterations; no globally bounded polynomial degree is asserted.
lem-filtered-graded-lie-algebra-defines-:
## Statement

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a cohomologically graded Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field: its degree-zero bracket is graded skew, satisfies graded Jacobi, and a degree-one map $d$ satisfies $d^2=0$ and $d[x,y]=[dx,y]+(-1)^{|x|}[x,dy]$. Suppose its degreewise separated complete positive filtration is preserved by $d$ and satisfies $[F^r\mathfrak g,F^s\mathfrak g]\subseteq F^{r+s}\mathfrak g$. With $s:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g[1]$ of degree $-1$, set

$$q_1(sx)=-s(dx),\qquad q_2(sx,sy)=(-1)^{|x|}s[x,y],\qquad q_n=0\ (n\ge3).$$

These operations define a complete filtered shifted L∞-algebra. Its degree-zero Maurer–Cartan elements are exactly $sR$, where $R\in F^1\mathfrak g^1$ satisfies $dR+[R,R]/2=0$. Its elementary gauge paths are exactly $R'=-d\xi+[\xi,R]$ with $\xi\in F^1\mathfrak g^0[t]^{\wedge}$, under $w=sR$, $a=s\xi$.
thm-filtered-l-infinity-morphisms-preser:
## Statement

Let $f:W\to Z$ be a filtered L∞-morphism between complete filtered shifted algebras over a characteristic-zero field. It induces a map on Maurer–Cartan elements by [[thm-filtered-l-infinity-morphisms-preserve-maurer-cartan-elements]]. It carries every completed polynomial gauge path of [[def-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-path]] to such a path and preserves its endpoints. Consequently it induces a map on the equivalence classes generated by those paths. These induced maps preserve identities and composition.

Put $P=F^1W$, with its complete induced filtration, and similarly $P'=F^1Z$. Scalar extension below is on these positive ideals. More explicitly use right-placed forms, $\Omega=k[t,dt]$, $|t|=0$, $|dt|=1$, $d(t)=dt$, $(dt)^2=0$, and the completion

$$P\widehat\otimes\Omega=\varprojlim_N((P/F^NW)\otimes\Omega).$$

Let $w(t)\in F^1(P\widehat\otimes k[t])^0$ and $a(t)\in F^1(P\widehat\otimes k[t])^{-1}$ satisfy

$$c_q(w(t))=0,\qquad w'(t)=q_1^{w(t)}(a(t)),\qquad q_1^w(a)=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{q_{n+1}(w^n,a)}{n!}.$$

Then their image path and parameter are

$$u(t)=f_*(w(t)),\qquad b(t)=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{f_{n+1}(w(t)^n,a(t))}{n!},$$

and satisfy $c_r(u(t))=0$, $u'(t)=r_1^{u(t)}(b(t))$, with endpoints $u(0)=f_*(w(0))$ and $u(1)=f_*(w(1))$. Each coefficient function is polynomial modulo every $F^N$; no common bound on its polynomial degree is assumed. The assertion includes the unique flows of [[lem-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-equation-has-unique-complete-polynomial-flow]].

For clarity, extension to an arbitrary commutative dg scalar algebra $A$ is part of the assertion. With $P$ factors placed before scalar factors and homogeneous $x_i\in P$, $a_i\in A$, the shifted operations and morphism coefficients on $P\widehat\otimes A$ are

$$q_1^A(x\otimes a)=q_1(x)\otimes a+(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes d_Aa,$$

$$q_n^A(x_1\otimes a_1,\ldots,x_n\otimes a_n)=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|a_i||x_j|}q_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\otimes a_1\cdots a_n\quad(n\ge2),$$

$$f_n^A(x_1\otimes a_1,\ldots,x_n\otimes a_n)=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|a_i||x_j|}f_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\otimes a_1\cdots a_n\quad(n\ge1).$$

These define complete filtered shifted L∞-algebras and a filtered morphism, natural in dg algebra maps $A\to B$. Their Maurer–Cartan pushforwards satisfy the same curvature and composition formulas as over the original field. This restriction is essential when the original filtration bounds do not control inputs outside $F^1W$.
thm-maurer-cartan-elements-classify-fixe:
## Statement

Use [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]], and put $\mathfrak g=F^1\mathfrak l$, $d=[D,-]$. Then

$$R\longmapsto D+R$$

is a bijection between $\{R\in\mathfrak g^1:dR+[R,R]/2=0\}$ and all the stated fixed-carrier codifferential deformations. It identifies their equivalence classes by all allowed coalgebra automorphisms with Maurer–Cartan gauge classes of the shifted filtered L∞-algebra of [[lem-filtered-graded-lie-algebra-defines-a-shifted-l-infinity-algebra]], using [[def-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-path]].

More explicitly, the full allowed group is $\exp(\mathfrak g^0)$, with group operation inherited from composition, and its action on Maurer–Cartan elements is

$$R\longmapsto e^{\operatorname{ad}_X}R-\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{(\operatorname{ad}_X)^j(dX)}{(j+1)!},\qquad X\in\mathfrak g^0.$$

The gauge-path relation, including variable parameters, equals the orbit relation of this action. No assertion that an unspecified deformation problem is governed by an arbitrary L∞-algebra is included.

For the tensor carrier on $A[1]$, this is the fixed-carrier A∞-structure correspondence in the native unsuspended convention, using [[lem-unsuspended-a-infinity-identities-are-tensor-codifferentials]], including its morphism signs. For the symmetric carrier on $V[1]$, it is the fixed-carrier L∞ correspondence in [[def-shifted-coalgebra-l-infinity-algebra]]. Both identifications are coefficient-complete and retain every allowed identity-modulo-ideal equivalence.
thm-unital-associative-deformations-are-:
## Statement

Let $(A,\mu,e)$ be any unital associative $k$-algebra concentrated in degree zero, with no finite-dimensionality hypothesis. Let $B,I$ satisfy [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]], put $M=\varprojlim_n A\otimes_k B/I^n$, and take $C=T^c(A[1])$. Let $s:A\to A[1]$ have degree $-1$. The binary Taylor map

$$b_\mu(sa,sb)=s\mu(a,b)$$

extends to a degree-one square-zero coderivation $D$ of $C_B$. Let $\mathfrak n\subseteq\mathfrak l$ be the coderivations whose Taylor maps vanish whenever one unsuspended argument is $e$. Then $(F^1\mathfrak n,[D,-],[-,-])$ is a complete filtered differential graded Lie algebra.

Its Maurer–Cartan elements are exactly the continuous $B$-bilinear associative products $\mu+\alpha$ on $M$, reducing to $\mu$ modulo $I$, with the same specified unit $e$. Its gauge classes are exactly their classes under all continuous $B$-linear changes of variables $g\equiv\operatorname{id}\pmod I$ satisfying $g(e)=e$, acting by

$$m'(a,b)=g\bigl(m(g^{-1}a,g^{-1}b)\bigr).$$

For $B=k[\![h]\!]$, $I=(h)$, this includes the formal products $a\star b=ab+\sum_{j\ge1}h^jB_j(a,b)$ with $B_j(e,a)=B_j(a,e)=0$, including [[def-formal-associative-deformation-of-a-commutative-algebra]] when the initial product is commutative. No commutativity is required of the deformed products.

The exact extension to a graded product of degree zero, with the same cohomological suspension, is $b_\mu(sa,sb)=(-1)^{|a|}s\mu(a,b)$. The statement about strict product classes above concerns ordinary degree-zero $A$; for graded $A$ higher Taylor components can have degree zero and strict changes of variables require the unary subgroup.
